primary.key: I, O Gudakesha, am the Self, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.
primary.s: Granting Arjuna’s plea for his glories, Krishna names this first, ahead of the chief of each kind; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), Gītā Bhāṣya 10.20, reads it as the Lord seated as soul in beings who form his body, and so their support, ruler and master.
primary.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 10.20, A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

basis.words: In the hearts of all beings, who constitute My body, I am seated as their Atma (Soul)—To be the Atma is indeed to be in every manner the Support, the Ruler and the Master.
basis.gloss: The Lord is seated as the soul (ātman) in the hearts of all beings, and those beings are his body; to be their soul is to be, in every way, their support, their ruler and their master.

standby.key: Out of pure compassion for them, dwelling within their Self, I destroy the ignorance-born darkness by the shining lamp of wisdom.
standby.s: Krishna, speaking of devotees who delight in talking of him, says what more he does for them; Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 10.11, reads the darkness as illusory knowledge from want of discrimination, and the lamp as discriminating knowledge fed by devotion and fanned by meditation.
standby.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 10.11, A. Mahadeva Sastri, The Bhagavad-Gita with the Commentary of Sri Sankaracharya, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

basis.words: destroy the darkness of ignorance, — that illusory knowledge which is caused by the absence of discrimination, — by the lamp of wisdom, by the lamp of discriminatory knowledge, fed by the oil of pure Devotion (Bhakti-pras&da), fanned by the wind of earnest meditation on Me
basis.gloss: The darkness of ignorance is the illusory knowledge that arises when discrimination is absent; the Lord destroys it with the lamp of wisdom, which is discriminating knowledge, fed with the oil of pure devotion and fanned by the wind of earnest meditation on him.
